A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NMWPM research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, supporting reliable comparison despite substantial additions and rearrangement.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 report original simulated decoding results, including logical error rates, thresholds and learned weight distributions for toric and rotated surface codes.

after.justification: v2 retains original decoding results and adds circuit-level simulations, ablations, transfer and extrapolation experiments, and inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: The GNN–Transformer predictor, BCE-plus-entropy objective and matching inference remain. Section 4.4 revises the stated rotated-code label-construction procedure from repeatedly matching with varying virtual-node counts to introducing a virtual node for an odd-endpoint cluster. Appendix D otherwise presents boundary features as implementation clarification.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates toric and rotated surface codes under independent and depolarizing noise. v2 adds repetition-code decoding under circuit-level noise (Figure 3) and a rotated surface-code X-memory circuit experiment (Appendix H). These introduce measurement-round and circuit-noise conditions absent from v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds correlated MWPM, labeled MWPM-Corr, to the corresponding toric and rotated depolarizing-noise comparisons in Figure 2. Alongside the retained MWPM, BPOSD-2 and QECCT comparators, this introduces a substantive correlation-aware classical alternative directly relevant to NMWPM's motivation. Appendix F separately supplies literature-reported threshold comparisons, without establishing matched reruns.

E3.justification: v2 extends retained evaluations to toric distance 12 and rotated distance 9. New protocols include circuit experiments with measurement rounds equal to distance, distance-4 ablation controls, distance-10-to-8 Transformer transfer with 20 fine-tuning epochs, and inference-time benchmarking. The original main architecture and optimizer settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained weight-distribution analysis, Section 6.3 tests geometric features, edge features, entropy regularization, maximum versus minimum aggregation, and replacing the Transformer with an MLP. Section 6.2 and Appendix E add extrapolation outside the training noise range and transfer across code distances. Appendix C also quantifies labeling fallback and filtering.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for decoder performance. The predicted-probability distributions concern model outputs, not statistical uncertainty in the reported performance estimates.

E6.justification: v2 retains the 17.9% and 10.95% toric thresholds but adds a 17.7% rotated-code threshold and extensive circuit, ablation, transfer, extrapolation and timing results. The reported rotated distance-7 comparison changes from approximate QECCT parity to a small NMWPM advantage. New Table 1 lists 6.64M QECCT parameters at distance 10, conflicting with the 6.71M stated in both versions' prose.

T1.justification: The substantive background definitions, matching objective, training objective and complexity analysis are retained. Several standard sublayer formula expansions are condensed into prose and notation is adjusted, but no new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The architecture, supervised-training and hybrid-decoding contribution claims remain. The abstract replaces its general LER-improvement statement with near-bound threshold claims, but describes both 17.9% and 10.95% as depolarizing-noise results. Section 5.2 still identifies 10.95% as the independent-noise threshold, creating a limited but substantive scope error in the headline claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking ablations to the roles of self-attention, entropy regularization and asymmetric edge signals. It interprets transfer results as evidence of features that generalize across code distances and explains how heuristic labels differ from shortest-path matching. It also discloses the GPU-memory limitation preventing QECCT evaluation at distance 12.

D1.justification: Appendices C–E disclose the 10-second labeling timeout, training-only sample filtering, first-valid-matching label selection, virtual-boundary-node features, and nine training versus eighteen evaluation noise levels. v2 also adds a linked source-code reference and details the new GPU/CPU timing benchmark. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused references covering correlated and recursive MWPM, Stim, quantum LDPC codes and additional neural decoders; Appendix F broadens literature-threshold positioning. The Celikkanat citation is removed. The central positioning of a neural predictor augmenting classical matching remains, while several other bibliography changes merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain. v2 condenses background and method explanations, merges evaluation metrics with results, shortens the weight-distribution discussion, and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement. Appendix organization expands, but the retained exposition undergoes localized compression rather than wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: v1 Figures 2–4 are consolidated and expanded into the ten-panel v2 Figure 2. Separate weight-distribution plots become an overlay, and new circuit-noise and ablation plots and six tables are added. The existing architectural schematic is retained but reduced to a column-sized display. These substantially change the visual organization.

improvement.justification: v2 materially addresses v1's limited validation of component choices and applicability through ablations, a correlation-aware comparator, circuit-noise experiments, transfer tests and measured runtime. Detailed labeling and boundary disclosures plus a source-code link also strengthen reproducibility. These gains outweigh the new abstract noise-model misstatement and parameter-count inconsistency, although statistical uncertainty remains unreported.
